targets.summary: This code should be made headeronly (living in torch/headeronly) and re-exposed from the c10 side so the long-term behavior is correct.
targets.evidence: Before the change, the commented line was `using c10::is_complex;` (alongside `using c10::scalar_value_type;`). It sat inside `HIDDEN_NAMESPACE_BEGIN(torch, headeronly)`, so it only pulled the c10 definitions into the headeronly namespace. In the merged code those `using` lines are gone. The definitions themselves moved: `namespace c10 {` became `HIDDEN_NAMESPACE_BEGIN(torch, headeronly)` and `} // namespace c10` became `HIDDEN_NAMESPACE_END(torch, headeronly)`. So `is_complex` and `scalar_value_type` are now defined in torch/headeronly itself instead of being aliased from c10, which is what the maintainer asked for. The other half of the request, re-exposing them on the c10 side, presumably happens in a c10 header that isn't part of this diff.
